nce_001: You can recognise it by its grid-patterned rows of olive trees, unchanged since 1546, growing beside the ruins of a Roman amphitheatre. It stands in the Jardin du Monastere de Cimiez.
nce_003: You can recognise them by the ten plane trees standing among a mix descended from the garden's original 1851 planting list. They stand in the Jardin Albert 1er.
nce_005: You can recognise them by the dark, vertical cypress silhouette rising over the terraced graves, visible from the bay below. They stand in the Cimetiere du Chateau.
nce_006: You can recognise them by the mix of palms, evergreen oaks, carob trees and pines lining the seafront path. They stand along the Promenade des Anglais.
nce_007: You can recognise them by the tall palms rising at each corner of the garden's three formal flowerbeds. They stand in the Jardin du Musee Massena.
nce_008: You can recognise it as the specimen credited with bringing its species to France, standing in what is left of a once-vast tropical estate. It stands in Parc Vigier.
nce_010: You can recognise it in autumn by carrying flowers and red, strawberry-like fruit on its branches at the same time. It stands in the gardens of the Chateau de Cremat.
